title: Retroactive Authorization of Services Already Performed — Referrals & Prior Authorizations
content:
A service that was performed without the authorization its Referrals & Prior Authorizations type requires may be authorized retroactively where the type has a retroactive window above zero (urgent imaging and procedures, and in-group referrals).

## Rule

1. The retroactive request is made no later than the type's retroactive window counted from the date of service of the visit, which is the scheduled date on the appointment record of that visit.
2. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the date of service, and a request on the last day still qualifies.
3. An approved retroactive request grants units, with the reason retroactive authorization, equal to the services it covers, and those services then use the units.
4. A service outside the window, or on a type with no retroactive window, stays unauthorized; the group, not the insured patient, bears that denial under the Patient Financial Account rules.

## Window boundaries (hypothetical dates of service)

| Retroactive window | Date of service | Last day a request qualifies | Request on | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14 days | 2026-02-20 | 2026-03-06 | 2026-03-06 | within the window |
| 14 days | 2026-02-20 | 2026-03-06 | 2026-03-07 | outside — the service stays unauthorized |
| 7 days | 2026-02-20 | 2026-02-27 | 2026-02-27 | within the window |
| 7 days | 2026-02-20 | 2026-02-27 | 2026-02-28 | outside — the service stays unauthorized |

Day 1 of each window is 21 February, the day after the date of service.

## Points of judgement

- *Who bears a service that stays unauthorized because the window has passed?* The group bears the denial, not the insured patient.
- *How many units does an approved retroactive request grant?* Units equal to the services it covers, and those services use them.
